how: A member proposes the small patch and others assent to its placement plan and a sub tag
Calls recruit helpers, ask members to spread the word, and seek visibility through a neighboring post
Two available people and the prospect of fighting overwhelming numbers make limited capacity explicit without establishing universal withdrawal
Members debate contrasting centers, convenient colors, box dimensions, and whether to retain the recognized pattern
Members announce a start and report that they are saving the boxes
Landmark and border instructions locate work without an evidenced agreed coordinate map or pixel template
Inviting someone to help run the sub and asking for consensus place this case among those with decided order without testing the cross-room frequency
A request for consensus and reluctant acceptance establish deliberation but do not establish a formal ballot or binding voting procedure
A bare assent answers the invitation to help run the sub
Two people using two accounts and a proposed duplicated-tab test do not establish productive scripts, bots, or spare accounts
A duplicated-tab glitch is proposed to test a design rather than demonstrated as extra productive placing capacity
A participant quitting for the night is answered by another promising to maintain the boxes with two people
Reporting a hit from the Bolivian flag supplies limited attribution without establishing an investigation of individual placers or intentions
Neighbors settle non-destruction, expendable background, possible moves, and a line the other party should police
Members explicitly promise not to touch neighboring art and to protect an existing design
Members call for help to a neighbor, a visitor reports making boxes, and another visitor asks for help against a raid
Members carry contact and proposals across room boundaries before using neighboring space or requesting relocation
Coalition invitations and reported expected assistance establish contact but leave membership and delivered collective protection unresolved
A requested overlap is accepted while an unannounced intruder is redirected, showing permission over a claimed patch without proving continuing host administration
Members weigh ceding against fighting and one reports beginning to move after the relocation offer
Relocation includes refusing to abandon the first-held patch before reconsidering the offer under unequal pressure
Moving can begin while original boxes remain, so relocation need not await complete erasure or eliminate attachment to the original patch
Requesting group consensus and refusing relocation do not establish a dispute over who may bind other placers
Reported damage and attachment to the first-held patch do not establish a quarrel inherited from before the canvas
Calling the boxes a nation and declaring the sub will live on do not establish an inherited collective body or color doctrine
Friendly self-positioning and reported damage do not identify a preexisting tie supplying an attack target
Thanking the maker of the sub establishes the element's minimal form of opening a canvas venue
Proposing boxes and acknowledging the new sub do not establish fake news, parody, or takeover framing
Members express pride, praise the effort, and claim their own labor on the surviving work
Participants preserve a triumph picture, identify a surviving box, recall the starting patch, and point to a video
Statements that the sub remains and will live on express minimal intended continuity without establishing a new purpose or subsequent activity
Questions about a surviving box's origin and the answer locating the starting patch do not establish contested cleanup or an authoritative version
A visitor admits encroachment, but defensive calls and reclamation talk do not establish an attack directed by the host room
Remembering a proper battle does not establish rival-directed taunts, victory claims, salutes, or a continuing spoken contest
The initial patch proposal precedes requests for helpers around work already underway, supporting the sequence without isolating its causal mechanism
Recruitment accompanies pride in work already done, so a call cannot explain every preceding placement or demonstrate which later placing answered it
Reports of saved boxes precede an explicit overnight maintenance handoff, supporting upkeep of existing work without isolating the effect of the report
A proposed boundary around surviving squares and the arrival of competing builders explicitly connect protection with negotiating a line
Negotiation also permits prospective overlap, so erosion is one route into border talk rather than a necessary prior event
An explicit promise not to touch neighboring art directly accepts the truce proposal, establishing agreed restraint without verifying every placer's compliance
Maintenance strain does not itself establish machine escalation when the only capacity statement is two people and two accounts
Pride marks partial work while helpers are still being recruited, so celebrating does not require a reported completed design
Calling a picture the group's big triumph combines celebration and preservation in one act rather than establishing a causal progression between them
Preserving a triumph picture and declaring that the sub remains do not show the record causing a later purpose or activity
Unequal numbers prompt deliberation after an explicit refusal rather than automatically ending defense, and movement can leave some original boxes intact
Design disagreement can settle by retaining the recognized existing pattern rather than by posting a new template
The clearest bare joining reply accepts helping run the sub, which does not itself demonstrate answering a placement call or every reader's obligation to answer
Requests under strain can fail, and later reported help must be distinguished from unverified delivery after a plea
A truce precedes a call to help and a neighbor later reports making boxes, supporting a channel to assistance without establishing an obligatory exchange
A recruitment call and later defensive encouragement do not establish recruited hands turning against a rival's work
The explicit restraint answers a truce proposal rather than a demonstrated call by the room to attack
A visitor's relocation request and the room's refusal do not identify a host attack call that caused negotiation
A retrospective battle reference does not show an attack call causing a rival-directed spoken contest
An invitation and expected council assistance do not establish coalition membership, a shared threat, or delivered mutual defense
A canvas venue is acknowledged at the start without evidence that recruitment flooded a parent sub or caused its moderators to segregate the talk
Negotiating movement and asking for consensus do not establish that members contested anyone's authority to commit the group
